title: Review: Series and parallel circuits; Kirchhoff's laws; Potential dividers; EMF and internal resistance; Capacitance and capacitor energy

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: emf
items.clue: Energy transferred to each coulomb of charge by the source.

items.label: Short circuit
items.clue: Connection with R = 0, giving a very large current that heats the cell.

items.label: Capacitance
items.clue: Quantity for parallel plates that is proportional to area A and to 1/d.

items.label: Internal resistance
items.clue: Property r of a real cell, treated as sitting in series with an ideal cell.

questions.stem: A 15 V supply charges a 12 V battery. They are connected in a single loop, positive terminal to positive terminal, and the total resistance in the loop is 2.0 Ω. What is the current, and which way does it pass through the battery?

options.text: 13.5 A, in at the battery's negative terminal and out at its positive terminal
7.5 A, in at the battery's positive terminal and out at its negative terminal
1.5 A, in at the battery's positive terminal and out at its negative terminal
1.5 A, in at the battery's negative terminal and out at its positive terminal

questions.explanation: Right. Net emf = 15 − 12 = 3.0 V, so I = 1.5 A. The larger emf wins and drives current backwards through the battery: that is charging.

questions.stem: An LDR and a 10 kΩ fixed resistor are in series across a 6.0 V supply of negligible internal resistance. An ideal voltmeter is connected across the fixed resistor. The LDR's resistance is 50 kΩ in the dark and 1.0 kΩ in bright light. What does the voltmeter read in each case?

options.text: 5.0 V in the dark; 0.55 V in bright light
5.5 V in the dark; 1.0 V in bright light
1.0 V in the dark; 5.5 V in bright light

questions.explanation: Dark: 6.0 × 10/(10 + 50) = 1.0 V. Bright: 6.0 × 10/(10 + 1.0) = 5.5 V. The fixed resistor's share rises as the LDR's resistance falls.

questions.stem: A battery of emf 9.0 V and internal resistance 0.50 Ω is connected to a 4.0 Ω resistor. What is the terminal potential difference of the battery?
Predict first. An uncharged parallel-plate capacitor is connected to a battery and left until it is fully charged. Which statement correctly describes how the capacitor becomes charged?

options.text: Electrons move from one plate, through the wires and battery, to the other plate.
Electrons cross the gap between the two plates, from one plate to the other.
The battery creates new charge and places some on each of the two plates.
The battery adds charge to one plate, and the other plate remains neutral.

questions.stem: An air-filled parallel-plate capacitor is charged and then disconnected from the supply. Its plates are then pulled apart to twice their separation. What happens to the charge on each plate, the potential difference across the capacitor and the energy it stores?

options.text: Charge unchanged; potential difference doubles; energy doubles.
Charge halves; potential difference unchanged; energy halves.
Charge unchanged; potential difference halves; energy halves.
Charge, potential difference and energy are all unchanged.

questions.explanation: Disconnected, the charge has nowhere to go: Q is fixed. C ∝ 1/d halves, so the potential difference Q/C doubles and the energy ½Q²/C doubles. The extra energy is the work done pulling the attracting plates apart.

questions.stem: Three cells are connected in series in a single line: two of emf 1.5 V face one way, and one of emf 2.0 V faces the other way. What is the total emf of the line?
questions.explanation: Right. 1.5 + 1.5 − 2.0 = 1.0 V, in the direction the two 1.5 V cells push.

questions.stem: An LDR and a 300 Ω resistor are in series across a 6.0 V supply of negligible internal resistance. In the room's light the LDR's resistance is 900 Ω. What does an ideal voltmeter across the 300 Ω resistor read?
questions.explanation: The pd divides in proportion to resistance: 6.0 × 300/(300 + 900) = 1.5 V.

questions.stem: A battery of internal resistance r is connected to an external resistor whose resistance equals r. The external resistor is then replaced by one of resistance 2r. How does the potential difference across the terminals of the battery change?

options.text: It stays equal to its first value.
It rises to 2 times its first value.
It falls to 2/3 of its first value.
It increases to 4/3 of its first value.

questions.stem: A parallel-plate capacitor is connected to an ideal 12 V battery. When the capacitor is fully charged, its positive plate carries a charge of 3.6 × 10⁻⁵ C. What is the capacitance of the capacitor?

An air-filled parallel-plate capacitor has a capacitance of 16 pF. A second air-filled parallel-plate capacitor has plates with three times the area of the first capacitor's plates, and its plates are twice as far apart. What is the capacitance of the second capacitor?

A 12 V dc supply of negligible internal resistance is connected to a 4.0 Ω resistor in series with a parallel combination of a 6.0 Ω resistor and a 12 Ω resistor. What is the current in the 12 Ω resistor?

A potentiometer has a uniform resistance track connected across a 9.0 V dc supply of negligible internal resistance. An ideal voltmeter is connected between one end of the track and the sliding contact, which is one third of the way along the track from that end. What does the voltmeter read?
